response_text:
Looking at this PR carefully, I need to evaluate the per-topic unsubscribe feature for real bugs, security issues, and other problems a maintainer would care about.

Key areas of concern:
1. The new `unsubscribe` controller action is a GET that mutates state
2. The template path doesn't align with the route name
3. Missing authorization and nil checks
4. Lack of tests for new functionality
5. Typo in controller method name

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/topics_controller.rb",
      "line": 98,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "CSRF: GET request mutates notification state",
      "body": "The `unsubscribe` action is wired to two GET routes (`get \"t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe\"` and `get \"t/:topic_id/unsubscribe\"` in config/routes.rb) and immediately mutates the user's `TopicUser.notification_level` based on `current_user.id`. Rails does not require a CSRF token for GET requests, so any logged-in user can be silently toggled off a topic by an attacker who embeds the unsubscribe URL in an image/link on a third-party site. The unsubscribe URL is also publicly linkable (no signed token), and the `before_filter :ensure_logged_in` does not help because the victim is already authenticated. This should be a POST (or require a signed token like `EmailUnsubscribeKey`), and ideally the state change should happen only after a user gesture."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/topics_controller.rb",
      "line": 105,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists",
      "body": "`tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` may return nil if the current user has no TopicUser record for that topic (e.g. they have never visited it). The very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, which will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil`. The action needs to handle the nil case, e.g. create the row or short-circuit, otherwise every unsubscribe from a never-visited topic raises a 500."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/topics_controller.rb",
      "line": 98,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "No authorization / visibility check on topic",
      "body": "Unlike the regular `show` action, `unsubscribe` never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (or any equivalent). `TopicView.new` is invoked with `current_user` but the action then loads/writes a `TopicUser` row for `params[:topic_id]` without verifying the topic exists, is not deleted, and is in a category the user is allowed to see. A user could be subscribed/muted on topics they should never have known about, and the response can leak topic state for topics in restricted categories."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs",
      "line": 1,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Template path does not match route registration",
      "body": "The route map registers a top-level route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` and a top-level view `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, but the template is placed at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. Ember resolves templates by dasherizing the route name, so `topicUnsubscribe` looks up `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`, not `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (which would belong to a nested `topic/unsubscribe` route that is not defined). The unsubscribe page will fail to render its body. Either nest the route under `topic` and move the template accordingly, or rename the template/view/controller files so the route, controller, view, and template all use the same `topicUnsubscribe` name."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/topics_controller.rb",
      "line": 98,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Unsubscribe toggles instead of muting from email",
      "body": "The toggle logic (`if tu.notification_level > :regular then :regular else :muted`) is appropriate for the on-site notification dropdown, but the link in the email is built via `post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and shown as \"To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here\". A user who is `:tracking` or `:watching` will be downgraded only to `:regular`, not muted, so the unsubscribe email doesn't actually stop notifications on the first click. Either the email link should target an endpoint that always mutes, or the toggle behavior should be reconsidered."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/topics_controller.rb",
      "line": 113,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Bypasses TopicUser.change side effects",
      "body": "The action writes the new notification level with `tu.save!`, instead of using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)`. As a result `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, and the `MessageBus.publish(\"/topic/#{topic_id}\", {notification_level_change: ...})` message that the rest of the app relies on are skipped. The client will not refresh its notification-level badge, and auditing/debugging of why a notification level changed is lost."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6",
      "line": 5,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "Typo in controller property name and template binding",
      "body": "The property is defined as `stopNotificiationsText` (note the doubled 'i') and is consumed by the template as `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`. While the template still resolves because both sides share the typo, this will trip future readers and any future rename attempt. The i18n key (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`) is correctly spelled, so the property should be `stopNotificationsText`."
    },
    {
      "file": "spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb",
      "line": 154,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests cover the new unsubscribe feature",
      "body": "The PR adds a new controller action, new routes, a new Ember route/controller/view/template, a new `Topic#unsubscribe_url` method, and includes the topic unsubscribe URL in notification emails. The only test change is adding `unsubscribe_url: \"/t/1234/unsubscribe\"` to an existing example and asserting `List-Unsubscribe` is present. There are no controller specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (CSRF/POST vs GET, slug redirect, nil TopicUser, permission check), no assertions that the email body actually contains the topic-specific unsubscribe link, and no assertion that `header_args['List-Unsubscribe']` carries the per-topic URL (RFC 8058). Without these the CSRF and behavior regressions above will not be caught."
    },
    {
      "file": "lib/email/message_builder.rb",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "List-Unsubscribe header ignores topic-specific URL",
      "body": "`header_args` only ever sets `List-Unsubscribe` to `<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>`, even though `@opts[:unsubscribe_url]` is now passed in from `user_notifications.rb`. Email clients use the `List-Unsubscribe` header for one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058); the topic-specific URL the PR just introduced is never used in the header, so the whole point of exposing `unsubscribe_url` to the builder is wasted for header-based unsubscribe."
    }
  ]
}
```

findings.title: CSRF: GET request mutates notification state
findings.body: The `unsubscribe` action is wired to two GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in config/routes.rb) and immediately mutates the user's `TopicUser.notification_level` based on `current_user.id`. Rails does not require a CSRF token for GET requests, so any logged-in user can be silently toggled off a topic by an attacker who embeds the unsubscribe URL in an image/link on a third-party site. The unsubscribe URL is also publicly linkable (no signed token), and the `before_filter :ensure_logged_in` does not help because the victim is already authenticated. This should be a POST (or require a signed token like `EmailUnsubscribeKey`), and ideally the state change should happen only after a user gesture.

findings.title: NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` may return nil if the current user has no TopicUser record for that topic (e.g. they have never visited it). The very next line dereferences `tu.notification_level`, which will raise `NoMethodError: undefined method 'notification_level' for nil`. The action needs to handle the nil case, e.g. create the row or short-circuit, otherwise every unsubscribe from a never-visited topic raises a 500.

findings.title: No authorization / visibility check on topic
findings.body: Unlike the regular `show` action, `unsubscribe` never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)` (or any equivalent). `TopicView.new` is invoked with `current_user` but the action then loads/writes a `TopicUser` row for `params[:topic_id]` without verifying the topic exists, is not deleted, and is in a category the user is allowed to see. A user could be subscribed/muted on topics they should never have known about, and the response can leak topic state for topics in restricted categories.

findings.title: Template path does not match route registration
findings.body: The route map registers a top-level route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` and a top-level view `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, but the template is placed at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`. Ember resolves templates by dasherizing the route name, so `topicUnsubscribe` looks up `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`, not `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (which would belong to a nested `topic/unsubscribe` route that is not defined). The unsubscribe page will fail to render its body. Either nest the route under `topic` and move the template accordingly, or rename the template/view/controller files so the route, controller, view, and template all use the same `topicUnsubscribe` name.

findings.title: Unsubscribe toggles instead of muting from email
findings.body: The toggle logic (`if tu.notification_level > :regular then :regular else :muted`) is appropriate for the on-site notification dropdown, but the link in the email is built via `post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and shown as "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here". A user who is `:tracking` or `:watching` will be downgraded only to `:regular`, not muted, so the unsubscribe email doesn't actually stop notifications on the first click. Either the email link should target an endpoint that always mutes, or the toggle behavior should be reconsidered.

findings.title: Bypasses TopicUser.change side effects
findings.body: The action writes the new notification level with `tu.save!`, instead of using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)`. As a result `notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`, and the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", {notification_level_change: ...})` message that the rest of the app relies on are skipped. The client will not refresh its notification-level badge, and auditing/debugging of why a notification level changed is lost.

findings.title: Typo in controller property name and template binding
findings.body: The property is defined as `stopNotificiationsText` (note the doubled 'i') and is consumed by the template as `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`. While the template still resolves because both sides share the typo, this will trip future readers and any future rename attempt. The i18n key (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`) is correctly spelled, so the property should be `stopNotificationsText`.

findings.title: No tests cover the new unsubscribe feature
findings.body: The PR adds a new controller action, new routes, a new Ember route/controller/view/template, a new `Topic#unsubscribe_url` method, and includes the topic unsubscribe URL in notification emails. The only test change is adding `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to an existing example and asserting `List-Unsubscribe` is present. There are no controller specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (CSRF/POST vs GET, slug redirect, nil TopicUser, permission check), no assertions that the email body actually contains the topic-specific unsubscribe link, and no assertion that `header_args['List-Unsubscribe']` carries the per-topic URL (RFC 8058). Without these the CSRF and behavior regressions above will not be caught.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header ignores topic-specific URL
findings.body: `header_args` only ever sets `List-Unsubscribe` to `<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>`, even though `@opts[:unsubscribe_url]` is now passed in from `user_notifications.rb`. Email clients use the `List-Unsubscribe` header for one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058); the topic-specific URL the PR just introduced is never used in the header, so the whole point of exposing `unsubscribe_url` to the builder is wasted for header-based unsubscribe.
